item.title: MJR Morning Brief — November 3, 2026
item.description:
From Media Jobs Report, here's your latest media industry update.
Kentucky Educational Television is mourning the loss of longtime CEO Shae Hopkins, who died October 29. Hopkins spent 40 years with KET, including more than 17 years leading the statewide network. She had planned to retire at the end of this year. Under her leadership, KET expanded educational programming, workforce development and emergency communications. America's Public Television Stations praised her dedication to public broadcasting and her lasting legacy of service.
In radio news,
Mentoring and Inspiring Women in Radio and the NAB Leadership Foundation have extended the application deadline for their 2026 LAUNCH Mentorship Program to November 13. Sponsored by Mr. Master, the year-long program supports women pursuing careers in broadcast engineering and technical operations. For the first time, women working for broadcast technology partners and vendors are also eligible. Applications are available at RadioMIW.com.
Turning to television,
Nexstar Media Group and Mission Broadcasting will bring all 12 Texas high school football state championship games to fans December 16th through 19th. The games, played at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, will air on participating television stations and streaming platforms across Texas. For the first time, fans outside the state can also stream the championships from anywhere.
In media technology news,
RCS Worldwide has named Tammy Halcomb Senior Vice President of Products and Merideth Kelly Senior Vice President of Global Client Experience and Transformation. Halcomb has held product leadership roles at Gemini XIII, WideOrbit and Marketron. Kelly joins from WideOrbit, where she most recently served as Vice President of Strategic Solutions.
And finally,
Sinclair has promoted 15-year company veteran Jennifer Lopez to Vice President and General Manager of its three Boise television stations, KBOI, KYUU and KNIN. Lopez returns to Boise after serving as General Sales Manager of KOMO and KUNS in Seattle since 2023. She will oversee station operations, sales, strategic planning and community engagement. Sinclair says her leadership experience and familiarity with the Boise market make her an ideal choice.
For more media news, the latest jobs, free media tools and more, log in to MediaJobsReport.com.
